### Modifications in Each File

1. **`xe_preempt_fence.c`**
   - Changed the work queue used for preempt fence waiting from `system_unbound_wq` to a device private work queue `q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq`. This modification ensures that preempt fences do not starve other users of the system-wide unbound work queue.

2. **`xe_device.c`**
   - Added the allocation of a new ordered work queue `preempt_fence_wq` for handling preempt fences during device creation. This queue is initialized with `alloc_ordered_workqueue`.
   - Included a check to ensure that the `preempt_fence_wq` is successfully allocated, along with existing checks for other work queues. If allocation fails, an error message is logged.
   - Added a cleanup step in the `xe_device_destroy` function to destroy the `preempt_fence_wq` when the device is destroyed.

3. **`xe_device_types.h`**
   - Introduced a new member `preempt_fence_wq` in the `xe_device` structure to hold the reference to the preempt fence work queue.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the three files are interconnected to enhance the handling of preempt fences in the DRM driver for Intel GPUs. The key relationships are:

- The introduction of the `preempt_fence_wq` in `xe_device_types.h` provides a dedicated work queue for preempt fence operations, which is crucial for avoiding starvation of the system-wide work queue.
- The allocation and management of this new work queue in `xe_device.c` ensure that it is properly initialized and cleaned up, maintaining resource integrity.
- The change in `xe_preempt_fence.c` to utilize this new work queue directly addresses the issue of potential starvation by ensuring that preempt fence operations are handled in a controlled manner, thus improving overall system responsiveness and stability. 

Overall, these modifications collectively aim to improve the efficiency and reliability of preempt fence handling in the driver.

Here is the commit message:
drm/xe: Use ordered wq for preempt fence waiting

Preempt fences can sleep waiting for an exec queue suspend operation to
complete. If the system_unbound_wq is used for waiting and the number of
waiters exceeds max_active this will result in other users of the
system_unbound_wq getting starved. Use a device private work queue for
preempt fences to avoid starvation of the system_unbound_wq.

Even though suspend operations can complete out-of-order, all suspend
operations within a VM need to complete before the preempt rebind worker
can start. With that, use a device private ordered wq for preempt fence
waiting.

 - Add comment about cleanup on failure (Matt R)
 - Update commit message (Lucas)

Fixes: dd08ebf6c352 ("drm/xe: Introduce a new DRM driver for Intel GPUs")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240401221913.139672-2-matthew.brost@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
(cherry picked from commit 37c15c4aae1fe3f67efd2641db8d8c25c2d524ab)
Signed-off-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that preempt fences can sleep while waiting for an execution queue suspend operation to complete. If the `system_unbound_wq` is used for this waiting and the number of waiters exceeds the maximum active limit, it can lead to starvation of other users of the `system_unbound_wq`, causing performance issues and potential deadlocks. This situation arises because suspend operations can complete out-of-order, and all suspend operations within a virtual machine (VM) need to finish before the preempt rebind worker can start.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool preempt_fence_enable_signaling(struct dma_fence *fence)
 {
 	struct xe_preempt_fence *pfence =
 		container_of(fence, typeof(*pfence), base);
 	struct xe_exec_queue *q = pfence->q;
 
 	pfence->error = q->ops->suspend(q);
-	queue_work(system_unbound_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
+	queue_work(q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
 	return true;
 }
